title: Lahaina water use permit applications and TIG report
summary: A board working group found that water use permit requests in the Lahaina management area total almost 9 million gallons a day, 213% of reported use, called sustainable yield numbers indefensible, and recommended joint review of surface and groundwater plus full monitoring before non-conditional permits. The board voted unanimously to approve the report and send it to CWRM, with a member saying the permit process is only partially complete and will need attention for years.

timeline.text: Members voted by raising hands, and the chair said the vote was unanimous and the motion passed.
The member said it will take attention over years, maybe decades, to fix some poor planning from the past.
The member said the permit process is just the beginning and is only partially complete.
The member said the report is meant as a reference for the board and the public as permitting goes forward.
The member said the process is very complicated, even for an expert in water.
A member said the report is meant to help the public understand a permit process that is hard even for experts.
A board member moved to approve the TIG report, and another member seconded the motion.
The approved report is to be sent to CWRM.
The chair said the board would vote to approve the report so it can be sent to CWRM.
The chair said the TIG presented its report to the board at the last meeting.
The board took up the TIG report on water use permit applications in the Lahaina surface and groundwater management area.
A member of the public was asked to send questions in writing to the board secretary before the next meeting.
Whether to accept or reject the report, or send the whole report or just a letter, will be decided at the next meeting.
Members are to write down questions and send them to the board secretary before the agenda posting deadline.
Counsel advised members to send written questions to the board secretary rather than contact group members individually, because of open-meeting rules.
At the next meeting, the board will be able to ask questions, discuss and vote on the report.
The group recommended a full water monitoring program before the state issues non-conditional water use permits.
The group recommended that surface water and groundwater applications be reviewed together, not in separate batches.
The group called the sustainable yield numbers (estimates of how much water can safely be used) indefensible as regulatory rules.
The group said the requests are basically incapable of being satisfied with existing surface water.
Total requests are almost 9 million gallons a day, which is 213% of reported existing use.
That application asks for 1.6 million gallons a day but claims to return 3 million, with no explanation.
One application, number 6065, requests 1.6 million gallons a day but claims a return of 3 million gallons a day.
The group found nothing objectionable in the applications except one.
The group said this batch held only surface water applications, but surface water and groundwater must be judged together.
